hens_rule_text: Up to 25 chickens per premises are allowed, though the number kept must be reasonable for the size of the property.
permit_notes: No permit is required to keep backyard chickens. Eggs and meat produced by the birds cannot be sold.
setback_notes: Enclosures must be 50 ft from neighboring residences and also meet the setback requirements that apply to accessory structures generally.
coop_rules: Enclosures must have a solid floor of cement or other washable material unless the pen is 75 ft or more from the nearest neighbor's residence or place of business; the coop must be kept clean and sanitary and free of waste and pest buildup.
zoning_notes: Atlanta does not explicitly ban roosters, but persistent crowing (10 or more consecutive minutes) is treated as a noise nuisance under Sec. 18-11, with fines from $150 to $1,000, so roosters are allowed only if they do not trigger a noise complaint.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
code_section: Atlanta Municipal Code, Chapter 18 (Animals), Sec. 18-7 to 18-41

sources.name: Atlanta, Ga. Code of Ordinances, Chapter 18 Animals
Farmland Information Center, Atlanta Georgia Urban Livestock Ordinances
Atlanta 311, Livestock/Farm Animals on Residential & Commercial Property

research_notes: Municode is region blocked from this machine; facts come from search-result extracts citing specific sections (18-7, 18-11, 18-41) plus a Farmland Information Center legal summary and the city's own 311 knowledge article, which agree on the 25-bird cap, 50 ft setback and no-permit rule. Rooster status is marked conditional because crowing itself is regulated as a noise nuisance rather than the bird being banned outright.
